propositions: Four AST guard tests pin `ast.parse`/`inspect.getsource` scans to hardcoded single files; subsequent module refactors moved the policed constructs to sibling modules, leaving guards scanning empty populations with zero matches.

Guards at applier_repair_property, llm_timeouts, probe_capability_heldout, and usage_log_pricing fail to detect violations because their scan targets no longer contain the constructs they police (measured: 0 matches in each scanned file).
Surviving guards prove the fix pattern: explicit anti-vacuity assertions checking that the scan population is non-empty (e.g. test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout:630 and test_web_tool_gating:130).

Repairs required: retarget guards to scan all modules where constructs now live, derive scan populations instead of hardcoding filenames, add anti-vacuity assertions with landmarks, and add mutation tests (plant violation in real module, verify guard turns RED).

Two additional findings (bedrock_provider, cloud_rate_limit_sweep_heldout) lack anti-vacuity assertions but are aimed correctly; one uses relative path not anchored to `__file__`; two are false positives or delegations.

All four primary vacuous guards (F1-F4) have been repaired with transitive closure scans and landmark-based anti-vacuity checks; mutation tests confirm repairs by planting violations in real homes and verifying guards RED before/after.
